Cosmic Ripple: When Holy Word: Serenity finishes its cooldown, you emit a burst of light that heals up to X injured targets within X yards for X.
Lash of Insanity: Void Tendrils summoned by Call to the Void generate X Insanity for you when they deal damage with Mind Flay.
Sinister Circulation: Successful Lethal Poison applications reduce the cooldown of Kingsbane by <X> sec.
Loaded Dice: Activating Adrenaline Rush improves the result of your next Roll the Bones by one level.
Seismic Storm: Earthquake damage has a X% chance to cause Seismic Lightning, dealing X Nature damage to the target.
Lashing Flames: Your Flametongue damage causes the target to take X% increased damage from your next Lava Lash. This effect stacks.
Deep Waters: X sec after casting Gift of the Queen, Sharas'dal casts another Gift of the Queen at the same location.
Thal'kiel's Ascendance: Demonic Empowerment has a X% chance to enrage Thal'kiel, causing each of your pets to deal X Shadow damage to its current target.
Flame Rift: Dimensional Rift can now summon a powerful Flame Rift.
Executioner's Precision: Attempts to finish off a foe, causing up to X Physical damage based on Rage spent. Only usable on enemies that have less than 20% health. If your foe survives, X% of the Rage spent is refunded.
Death and Glory: Odyn's Fury is empowered by either Odyn or Helya. Odyn empowers Odyn's Fury with X Fire damage and generates X Rage. Helya empowers Odyn's Fury with X Shadow damage which heals you for X% of the damage it deals.
Neltharion's Thunder: Thunderclap now applies Neltharion's Thunder, reducing your damage taken from the target by X%, stacking up to X times.
Create Item: Create a class set item appropriate for your loot specialization ().
Wild Thrash: The feral panic of being forced to shift causes the druid to thrash, inflicting X Spellstrike damage to all targets in X yards, and an additional X Spellstrike damage every X sec. for X. This effect stacks.
Gripping Chain: Fires a coiled chain at your enemy, pulling them to you.
Difficult Terrain: Moving around the stalagmite is difficult and causes you to move X% slower.
Test Insignia: Grants X reputation with a faction.
Fel Remanence: Remanence left behind by the Maiden's hammer inflicts X Fire damage every X sec. As the remanence decays, it emits Fel Echoes.
Whirlstorm: Invokes a Whirlstorm for X, drawing in enemies and inflicting Nature damage every second to enemies within X yards. This storm also sends out smaller Whirlstorms which also inflict Nature damage every second.
Tribes of Highmountain: The forces of Highmountain stand with the Legionfall Commander.
Call Up: Call a flight of Skyhorn Interceptors to strafe an area for physical damage.
Bursting Dreadflame: Inflicts X Fire damage to the targeted player and all other players within X yards.
Mega Kick: Knock the enemy far into the air.
Give Antidote: Give Fel Antidote Brew to a Fel Poisoned Initiate.
Netherlord's Brimstone Wrathsteed: Summons and dismisses your Netherlord's Brimstone Wrathsteed. This is a flying mount.
Netherlord's Accursed Wrathsteed: Summons and dismisses your Netherlord's Accursed Wrathsteed. This is a flying mount.
Rune of Valor: Odyn stands with the Legionfall Commander.
Light of the Dreamweaver: The forces of Val'sharah stand with the Legionfall Commander.
Fel Hardened Scales: The worm's scales are hardened with Fel energy, decreasing damage taken by X% per application.
Extinguish Life: After 30 stacks of Wrath of the Creators the maiden begins to extinguish all nearby life, inflicting X damage to all enemies with each cast.
Harden Fel Scales: Hardens the target's scales with Fel energy to prevent damage they take.
Weakened Scales: The worm's scales weaken, increasing damage taken by X% per application.
Fettering Fiction: Runes spring forth from the magical books, slowing all players.
Beguiling Biography: Entrancing narrative charms a random player. This effect breaks if their health goes below 30%.
Dreadstone: Your damaging and healing spells have a chance to increase your Mastery, Haste, or Critical Strike by X for X.
Shadow's Strike: Your damaging and healing spells have a chance to increase your Mastery, Haste, or Critical Strike by X for X.
Shadow Master: Your damaging and healing spells have a chance to increase your Mastery, Haste, or Critical Strike by X for X.
Focused Dreadflame: Inflicts X Fire damage to all players in a line in the direction of the targeted player, divided by the number of players hit.
Focused Dreadburst: Players affected by Focused Dreadflame explode, inflicting X Fire damage to themselves and all other players in X yards.
Throw Wyrmtongue Crate: Inflicts Physical damage to an enemy.
Mark of the Resistance: The forces of Suramar stand with the Legionfall Commander.
Fel Barbs: Your attacks have a chance to imbed Fel Barbs into your target, dealing X Fire damage over X.
Absorbing Elune's Power: Use Xal'atath to absorb remnants of Elune's power.
Grease the Gears: Increases your Haste by X for X.
Demonic Mending: Heals all nearby allies for X% of their max health.
Wildbrew: Raise a drink to the spirits, restoring X% health every X sec for X.
Hunter's Feast: Eat the feast, increasing Stamina and Agility by X% for X.
Fling Bone: Fling an eaten bone behind you, in true Vrykul tradition.
Vantus Rune: Tomb of Sargeras: Attune yourself to the energies of the targeted Tomb of Sargeras raid boss, increasing your Versatility by X when fighting that boss. This effect lasts for an entire week. You can only use one Vantus Rune per week.
Black Bile: Hurls a vial of black bile at an enemy, inflicting Shadow damage and reducing Haste by X%.
Poisoned by Fel: The totem's fel energies slow your abilities, and inflicts damage every second.
Mindwrack: The caster's mental torment manifests as physical pain in the body of its current threat target, inflicting X Physical damage and increasing Physical damage taken by X% for X.
Hateful Smash: Inflicts Physical damage to enemies in a line in front of the caster, stunning them for X.
Dark Bargain: Upon reaching 100 energy the Dark Young unleashes a profane ritual, increasing the damage taken, healing done and damage done of all creatures, including players, within X yards of the caster by X% for X. Any player reaching X stacks of becomes an unwilling thrall of G'huun, attacking their allies until they are brought to 50% of their maximum life.
Ripper Blade: Tears into an enemy's flesh with a savage blade, inflicting Physical damage immediately and Physical damage every sec.
Curse of Worms: Suffering from an ancient curse which causes worms to crawl from under your skin every X sec for X.
Wild Bellow: Bellows loudly, dealing Physical damage and confusing enemies for X. Also applies Wild Spirit.
Wild Spirit: Evoke the energy of Wild Spirits at the target location, dealing X Nature damage and apply Wild Mark to all enemy targets within the area for X. While the Wild Spirits are active, each damaging ability you or your pet use against a target in the area will strike up to X nearby targets for X Nature damage.
Wild Swipe: Swipe enemies in front of the caster, dealing Physical damage and causing them to bleed for X.
Wild Winds: The Manifested Monarch unleashes orbs of wind, players that come into contact with an orb are knocked away and suffer X Nature damage.
Stifling Satire: As the tomes open, all sound is magically absorbed into the ancient pages, silencing all players for X.
Spear of Vengeance: The caster hurls their spear through the air. When it lands a Spear of Vengeance is created, inflicting X Fire damage to all players within X yards of it.

Obsidian Krolusk: Summons and dismisses an Obsidian Krolusk.
Spider Call: The spider screeches, calling additional spiders down from the web.
Fel Skein: The life force of creatures in the Life Link is shared. Damage received by any of these creatures is copied to the other creatures in the Link.
Fragment Burst: Inflicts X damage to all players immediately, as well as X damage every X sec for X. Also applies Ravaged Soul.
Shadow Conduit: Summons a shadow conduit at an enemy target's location for X. All enemies within range of the conduit suffer X Shadow damage every second.
Throw Arcane Tome: Throws the Tome of Arcane Monstrosities, inflicting X Arcane damage to nearby enemies. If not killed quickly, it will summon an Arcane Horror.
Tormented Eruption: Concentrated torment erupts from the prisoner, inflicting X Fire damage to enemies within X yards of each impact.
Book of Eternal Winter: Throws the Tome of Eternal Winter, inflicting X Frost damage to nearby enemies and leaving a frost zone that stuns enemies that enter it for X.
Throw Frost Tome: Throws the Tome of Eternal Winter, inflicting X Frost damage to nearby enemies and leaving a frost zone that stuns enemies that enter it for X.
Spontaneous Fragmentation: Summons a Fragment of Creation or Fragment of Obliteration at the feet of a target enemy with an opposite infusion after X sec. The fragment will pursue the target for X. If not consumed, it will trigger Fragment Burst.
Gravity Squeeze: Inflicts X Shadow damage every X sec. The amount inflicted increases the longer the player remains affected by Gravity Squeeze. The missiles from Darkness of a Thousand Souls will be sucked into the rift rather than hitting them if players are standing close enough to the rift to be affected by Gravity Squeeze.
Tome of Everlasting Silence: Throws a tome of Everlasting Silence, inflicting X Shadow damage to nearby enemies. As the tomes open, all sound is magically absorbed into the ancient pages, silencing all players within the area of effect for X.
Throw Silence Tome: Throws a tome of Everlasting Silence, inflicting X Shadow damage to nearby enemies. As the tomes open, all sound is magically absorbed into the ancient pages, silencing all players within the area of effect for X.
Extracting: Use your Tailoring skill to carefully extract Starlight Thread from the bracers.
Unstitching: Use your Leatherworking skill to unstitch the armor, yielding powerful ancient hides.
Dyeing: Use your Leatherworking skill to dye the faded shroud.

Ceremonial Bonesaw: The Drust would often use various animals in their rituals, mostly for their organs. Bonesaws were pivotal in breaking through some of the larger animals' rib cages in order to extract the heart of the beast.
Ancient Runebound Tome: Tomes were often kept by the strongest of the Drust, preserving the incantations of their magics and serving as conduits for harnessing their power. Scholars have tried to translate the ancient language transcribed within these tomes, only to find themselves going mad as they furthered their understanding of what had been written.
Disembowling Sickle: Many tools have been discovered that the Drust used in their rituals. One such tool was a sickle, used for ripping through the bellies of their sacrifices, spilling their entrails and allowing the Drust to use their organs in dark rituals.
Jagged Blade of the Drust: Used for both combat and ancient ceremonies, the blades of the Drust are fearsome objects. When wielded by a Drust, this blade can quickly find it's way into any vital organ within a matter of seconds.
Ritual Fetish: When the Drust were first learning to attach souls into constructs, they used the bones of their dead as hosts. Once the ritual was complete, these fetishes were said to emanate an eerie blue light, presumably the essence of the soul's power made manifest.
Akun'Jar Vase: The Zandalari praise many powerful spirit gods known as the Loa. One of which is the great thunder lizard, Akunda, the loa of storms and new beginnings. He believes that the storm has the power to wash away regret and sorrow.
Urn of Passage: During the final era of the Council of Tribes, a blood plague broke out, killing thousands of trolls. It was deemed that the bodies, too polluted for proper burial, would instead be burned and kept in special urns. As time progressed, this method became commonplace among the Zandalari in disposing of their dead.
Rezan Idol: Throughout the ages, many kings have ruled over the Zandalari empire. Each one however, knew their place when it came to the great loa and offered their praise to the mightiest of all of them, Rezan. This loa honors deeds over words, but takes slights very seriously and had been known to harbor grudges.
High Apothecary's Hood: Practioners of alchemy among the Zandalari kept a tight society within the empire known as the "Shadra'Zan". Entrance into the guild included a ritual which would require the inductee to imbibe a potion made from their own blood. Should they withstand the effects, they were deemed worthy to learn the secrets kept within.
Bwonsamdi Voodoo Mask: To honor the loa of death, Zandalari would don these masks in their rituals and pray to him. Bwonsamdi in turn would either answer in kind, or curse them with pain, depending on his mood. Bwonsamdi himself is the protector of the dead and brings the spirits of any who worship him into his realm, "Da Other Side".

Blowgun of the Sethra: The trolls of the desert who worshipped Sethraliss used these blowguns to hunt their prey, be it beast, or troll. The poison the darts were dipped in would paralyze their prey, and within a minute, kill them. "The Prick of Sethraliss" was whispered to children in order to keep them in line, as was written in an ancient poem: "Should the young turn defiant, show anger or malice, the winds of Vol'Dun will bring the Prick of Sethraliss."
Croak Crock: During times of war, the Zandalari faced off against many powerful foes. Some, even, that they could not break. Their witchdoctors devised these cursed pots and through the use of powerful magic, summoned them at different locations within the enemy's encampment. Shortly after, a fountain of frogs would spring forth, causing a ruckus and confusing the enemy in the process. Little did they know that these frogs carried a plague with them that would quickly devastate their ranks and force them to retreat or surrender.
Intact Direhorn Hatchling: The Zandalari are regarded for their beast taming, and one of their greatest allies is that of the direhorn. Plated skin, with spikes protruding from various directions, this creature offered both protection for istelf and that of its master. It was custom for its future master to be the first to see it when it broke free from its shell.surrender.
Sanguinating Totem: After the great plague, there were still those who clung to the magics of the blood god. They tested their magics and perfected them. One such relic was a totem, which when concentrated upon, would drain not just the life from their enemies, but also their blood, infusing the caster with it and altering them in unusual ways. This was the dawn of who the Zandalari call, "The Blood Trolls".

The Drust created prisons for these souls for later use in their dark rituals, during which time the soul would suffer within Thros, and become a twisted version of what it once had been.
Dance of the Dead: When the Drust wished to enchant the minds of their enemies, or prey, they would often do so subtly by leaving small tokens around their targets. Curious objects, when focused on by the holder, would summon a haunting vision of a dancing spectre. This spectre would entrance all who watched it, rendering them docile and easy to dispatch.
Restored Revenant: As the Drust became more skilled at trapping souls within objects, so did they become more adept at creating constructs of death in which to trap the souls. Revenants are amongst the fiercest of these creatures. Stripped of memory and any semblance of self, their bodies constructed from pieces that can no longer decompose, these creatures never tire and will hunt their prey for all eternity.
Fetish of the Tormented Mind: This fetish was paramount for twisting the minds of their enemies, causing doubt to grow like a weed within the target, encroaching brighter thoughts. Those afflicted would question their motivations, their ideals, or their courage and would often find themselves at the end of a Drust blade before finally rediscovering their resolve.

Thousandbite Piranha: Thousandbite Piranha are an aggressive freshwater fish that will devour anything in sight! These freshwater swarms are found primarily in vast lakes and sprawling river systems across the Dragon Isles. They are especially active in areas such as The Ohn'ahran Plains and The Waking Shores.
Cerulean Spinefish: Cerulean Spinefish are a sturdy fish adorned with many sharp spines. These saltwater schools can be found primarily in the ocean and other bodies of water connected to it. They are especially active in areas such as the river openings around The Waking Shores.
Aileron Seamoth: Aileron Seamoth glide across the ocean floor and jet upwards when they suspect a tasty treat! These saltwater schools can be found primarily in the ocean and other bodies of water connected to it. They are especially active in areas such as Iskaara in The Azure Span.
Temporal Dragonhead: Temporal Dragonhead are a peculiar fish whose scales seem to displace forwards and backwards every few seconds. Keep your fingers away from their sharp snout! These freshwater schools can be found primarily in the vast lakes and sprawling river systems around the Dragon Isles. They are especially active in areas such as the Uktulut Backwater in The Waking Shores.
Scalebelly Mackerel: Scalebelly Mackerel are an incredibly common fish in the Dragon Isles. They are easily caught in all bodies of water. Tossing unused Scalebelly Mackerel back into the water is a routine exercise done by even the most experienced Anglers.
Islefin Dorado: Islefin Dorado are an elusive fish whose fin is said to resemble the Dragon isles. They are found in all bodies of water around the isles.
Shimmering Treasure: Shimmering Treasure can appear in all bodies of water across the Dragon Isles. These pools contain untold treasures and are what every angler hopes to stumble upon. Fishing in these pools significantly increases your chance for rare treasures.
Rimefin Tuna: Rimefin Tuna are a large, fatty fish coated in a thin layer of protective ice. The thick layer of fat protects their vital organs in below freezing temperatures. You can find these pools in especially frosty climates around the Dragon Isles. The Iskaara Tuskarr are experts in catching these kinds of special fish.
Magma Thresherl: Magma Threshers are a muscular fish with a hardened outer shell consisting of various minerals. You can find these pools in especially hot climates around the Dragon Isles. The Iskaara Tuskarr are experts in catching these kinds of special fish.
Prismatic Leaper: Prismatic Leapers are a curious, agile fish with scales that shimmer when caught in the light. These fish love to leap from the water and can be found at some of the highest points around the Dragon Isles. The Iskaara Tuskarr are experts in catching these kinds of special fish.

Overgrown Bubble Poppy: Bubble Poppy is a delicate herb that grows in the aquatic locales of the Dragon Isles. It grows along the rivers, coasts, and inside damp caves. Despite its unique appearance, the Bubble Poppy flower isn't particularly useful. Rather, the watery, fungal orb that forms at its base is where the real value lies. Some herbs that grow within the Dream have sentience, and will not take lightly to attempts to gather them. They will uproot and flee from their would-be gatherers, but those who are determined may still be able to gather materials from these creatures.

Mycobloom: Mycobloom is an extremely common fungus found on Khaz Algar. It can be found in practically any terrain, growing absolutely anywhere it can.
Lush Mycobloom: Mycobloom is an extremely common fungus found on Khaz Algar. It can be found in practically any terrain, growing absolutely anywhere it can. Some herbs grow particularly well and thrive for any number of reasons, regardless of climate or location. Herbalists who come across these rare nodes can retrieve additional usable materials.
Luredrop: A carnivorous plant found within the underground spaces of Khaz Algar; Luredrop uses small bioluminescent lights to draw in insects and other prey that it uses to thrive.
Orbinid: Khaz Algar is a host to many unique species of plants, and Orbinid is no different. This plant seems to absorb latent magic through its viscous orb, which can be utilized in various professions to make anything from salves to inks.
Blessing Blossom: The Blessing Blossoms of Khaz Algar may appear harmless at first glance, but be wary: they host a dangerous toxin that can leave you extremely ill. However, if properly prepared, Blessing Blossoms have numerous medicinal properties, and drinking tea served in their hoods is considered a delicacy.
Arathor's Spear: Found within the bright, outdoor spaces of Khaz Algar, Arathor's Spear is a hearty herb with numerous uses. Most noteworthy is that the fibers can be woven to make parchment, or when tightly packed and treated, a material akin to wood. This allows it to be used for anything from books, to bows, to staves.

Due to their proximity to the Coreway, some herbs have a more direct connection with the World Soul. This link has caused the herbs to partially crystallize. Any herbalist who happens to gather one of these herbs will gain a small blessing in addition to some Crystalline Powder.
Altered Mycobloom: Mycobloom is an extremely common fungus found on Khaz Algar. It can be found in practically any terrain, growing absolutely anywhere it can. Deep below the surface of Khaz Algar lies the Black Blood of the Old Gods. It has begun to pool, and its festering has had an adverse affect on the local flora. Herbs that have had the misfortune of growing near such an influence have become altered... more dangerous. Any herbalist who braves the depths to gather such a thing will have to deal with the dangers of the plant itself, but will gain Writhing Samples for their efforts.
Irradiated Mycobloom: Mycobloom is an extremely common fungus found on Khaz Algar. It can be found in practically any terrain, growing absolutely anywhere it can. Recent events have led to a large amount of arcane magic to leak into the soil of Khaz Algar. As was noted back on the Dragon Isles, flora tend to be susceptible to magical influences, and this situation is no different. Some herbs here have become irradiated with arcane energy, and gathering them will allow the herbalist to obtain some Leyline Residue for their troubles. What may happen with the unstable arcane energy that remains however, is another story...
Sporefused Mycobloom: Mycobloom is an extremely common fungus found on Khaz Algar. It can be found in practically any terrain, growing absolutely anywhere it can. The underground of Khaz Algar is filled with a menagerie of lifeforms, large and small, each with their own unique features and behaviors. One such lifeform is a species of magical spore, not too dissimilar from the ones found in Zaralek Cavern on the Dragon Isles. These spores, however, aren't as symbiotic. Gathering an herb that hosts these spores will grant some Viridescent Spores, but have also been noted to cause strange hallucinations. Proceed with caution.
Camouflaged Mycobloom: Mycobloom is an extremely common fungus found on Khaz Algar. It can be found in practically any terrain, growing absolutely anywhere it can. Herbs on Khaz Algar have taken on many different variations to adapt to their environment, but one evolution stands out as particularly fascinating. These herbs are camouflaged; completely invisible to the unassisted eye! Aspiring herbalists and alchemists have found ways to see them, but the fact that they managed to go undetected for so long is nothing short of astounding. While they have no extra usable materials to speak of, the herbs themselves are just as useful as their less roguish counterparts.

Most noteworthy is that the fibers can be woven to make parchment, or when tightly packed and treated, a material akin to wood. This allows it to be used for anything from books, to bows, to staves. Herbs on Khaz Algar have taken on many different variations to adapt to their environment, but one evolution stands out as particularly fascinating. These herbs are camouflaged; completely invisible to the unassisted eye! Aspiring herbalists and alchemists have found ways to see them, but the fact that they managed to go undetected for so long is nothing short of astounding. While they have no extra usable materials to speak of, the herbs themselves are just as useful as their less roguish counterparts.
Sporefused Arathor's Spear: Found within the bright, outdoor spaces of Khaz Algar, Arathor's Spear is a hearty herb with numerous uses. Most noteworthy is that the fibers can be woven to make parchment, or when tightly packed and treated, a material akin to wood. This allows it to be used for anything from books, to bows, to staves. The underground of Khaz Algar is filled with a menagerie of lifeforms, large and small, each with their own unique features and behaviors. One such lifeform is a species of magical spore, not too dissimilar from the ones found in Zaralek Cavern on the Dragon Isles. These spores, however, aren't as symbiotic. Gathering an herb that hosts these spores will grant some Viridescent Spores, but have also been noted to cause strange hallucinations. Proceed with caution.

Nature works in mysterious ways, but there is nothing natural about rocks covered in dynamite! Abnormally rich metal deposits spotted by "helpful" Engineers are sometimes rigged up for detonation for an easy yield, but they are often abandoned when the demolitionist come to their senses. Overload Crystallized: Overloading a crystallized deposit will momentarily attune you to the world, creating a portal to send you to another nearby deposit. Specialized miners will open a portal back after gathering at their destination.
Overload Weeping: Overloading weeping deposits will cause an immediate mutation to occur and change them into a dangerous creature. This creature can provide a healthy source of Writhing Samples.
Overload Explosives: Overloading mining deposits riddled with dynamite seems like a chaotic and foolish decision but is nonetheless a practice growing in popularity as more and more armed mining deposits are abandoned. Miners lacking in self-preservation that overload these deposits will have mere seconds to gather extra ore, whilst pondering all of the choices that lead to that moment.
Overload Webbed Deposits: Spindlespiders have a tendency to nest up against sturdy rocky outcroppings. While most miners would prefer to collect what they can without disturbing them, overloading a webbed deposit will dislodge many spindlespiders that will attempt to scurry away. Catching these is a great source of additional cloth!

Tranquility Bloom: The environmental factors and changes of Quel'Thalas and the surrounding regions has had a profound impact on the local flora, including even the humble Peacebloom. It is still a staple of local crafting and is utilized in a wide variety of recipes, and a recent strain that has adapted to those changes has been dubbed Tranquility Bloom.
Sanguithorn: Once only usable as an edible plant for fleeting magical power, recent evolutionary changes and alchemical breakthroughs with bloodthistle have led to its use across the professions. This more potent growth has come to be known as sanguithorn, and still boasts fearsome magical capabilities. Sanguithorn are known to tether themselves to rocks, either above or under the ground, so check for them in more rugged terrain.
Azeroot: The hearty earthroot plant has grown stronger in recent years. Difficult to gather, but just as potent in crafting, azeroot is key to many recipes in Quel'Thalas. This sturdy wooden herb can be found on or around trees in the Quel'Thalas region.

Because of these changes, this new offshoot of silverleaf has become known as argentleaf. Regularly found among other common foliage, it is a standard ingredient of many recipes and is thus highly sought after.

Upon gathering these primal herbs, they gift you with some of their energy in the form of an additional charge for your Skyriding abilities.

Gathering these wild herbs releases a burst of nature magic, giving rise to a group of hostile herb lashers that attempt to take vengeance!

One can also step through the tear if they so choose--who knows where they might end up?
Overload Wild Herb: The lands of Zul'Aman teem with wild nature magic connected with the Loa themselves. By overloading a Wild herb, the herbalist may challenge an Avatar of Halazzi, the Lynx Loa, in combat. Success in this trial results in a temporary but keen increase to Perception.

Cursed Argentleaf: The silverleaf of Quel'Thalas has grown more lustrous in recent years, gaining a unique sheen that allows anyone to recognize it at a glance. Because of these changes, this new offshoot of silverleaf has become known as argentleaf. Regularly found among other common foliage, it is a standard ingredient of many recipes and is thus highly sought after. The herb gives off a sinister aura as if the very roots are laced with malice. Gathering the plant will surely bring some relief to the land, but at what cost to the herbalist?
Cursed Azeroot: The hearty earthroot plant has grown stronger in recent years. Difficult to gather, but just as potent in crafting, azeroot is key to many recipes in Quel'Thalas. This sturdy wooden herb can be found on or around trees in the Quel'Thalas region. The herb gives off a sinister aura as if the very roots are laced with malice. Gathering the plant will surely bring some relief to the land, but at what cost to the herbalist?
Cursed Mana Lily: Another recent offshoot species, mana lily is a new variant of mageroyal. The latent magic present in the Quel'Thalas region has seeped into the mana lily, giving them potent properties for crafting. If you're ever gathering around bodies of water, you can expect to find mana lilies somewhere nearby. The herb gives off a sinister aura as if the very roots are laced with malice. Gathering the plant will surely bring some relief to the land, but at what cost to the herbalist?
Cursed Sanguithorn: Once only usable as an edible plant for fleeting magical power, recent evolutionary changes and alchemical breakthroughs with bloodthistle have led to its use across the professions. This more potent growth has come to be known as sanguithorn, and still boasts fearsome magical capabilities. Sanguithorn are known to tether themselves to rocks, either above or under the ground, so check for them in more rugged terrain. The herb gives off a sinister aura as if the very roots are laced with malice. Gathering the plant will surely bring some relief to the land, but at what cost to the herbalist?
Cursed Tranquility Bloom: The environmental factors and changes of Quel'Thalas and the surrounding regions has had a profound impact on the local flora, including even the humble Peacebloom. It is still a staple of local crafting and is utilized in a wide variety of recipes, and a recent strain that has adapted to those changes has been dubbed Tranquility Bloom. The herb gives off a sinister aura as if the very roots are laced with malice. Gathering the plant will surely bring some relief to the land, but at what cost to the herbalist?
